title: Uniform Inference for Spatially Confounded Slopes under Infill Asymptotics and Vanishing Cross-Covariance
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; clean math and decision panels passed with no findings, but paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4 and no bounded same-topic repair can lift it.
gap_reasons: The paper score is constrained by the narrow parametric model, the absence of a certified implementation or substantive application, and the compressed treatment of load-bearing arbitrary-design covariance-remainder and quadratic-form CLT bounds.
The lower bound comes from the regular independent A=0 subexperiment and therefore matches the rates without establishing that vanishing cross-tail adaptation creates a distinct minimax difficulty.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed the affine-stencil experiment, uniform profile inference through vanishing cross-tail amplitude, exact attained Gaussian-reference calibration, and matching root-N confidence-set diameter and N^-1 risk lower bounds; both final review panels passed with no findings. The result remained below field because its upper theorem is confined to a narrow no-nugget Matérn-one-half class, its lower bound uses the regular independent subexperiment rather than a new weak-tail minimax obstruction, and no certified implementation or substantive application was delivered. A terminating certified approximation to the continuum critical value remains an explicit open question.
tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes reduce the stated signed Mat\'ern cross-tail model to a finite-dimensional mean cone and yield uniform actual-design Gaussian inference through vanishing amplitude. On the narrow parametric Gaussian, quasi-uniform, no-nugget class, the profile construction has asymptotic observed-law coverage, root-\(N\) diameter, and root-\(N\) estimation risk. An exact complete-data Gaussian two-point argument matches the diameter and squared-risk rates; its converse transfers conditionally to every superclass that contains the same fixed-design independent Mat\'ern-one-half \(A=0\) subexperiment with a common nontrivial slope interval. The exact least-favorable critical value is mathematically attained; the sole residual open question is a terminating certified numerical approximation of its continuum maximum with a proved error bound.
gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results deliver Gaussian inference for scalar covariance combinations. They do not provide design-uniform slope inference when the observation-scale cross-tail is local to zero and its exponent is unidentified.
fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, residual-scale studentization, conservative uniform coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching honest lower bounds, while exposing attainable exact calibration as a sharply delimited open theorem.
